primaryReference.fact: Closing a dialog queues its close event on the user interaction task source; it is not the synchronous end of dialog.close().

finding: app.js openTask synchronously invalidates old selection, creates a new selection and starts detail loading. The close handler later invalidates selection unconditionally even if this same dialog has already reopened. Thus an old queued native close can invalidate a new open dialog and move its focus.
reproductionCandidate: Use actual dialog.close() and the existing task button activation in the same evaluate task, then wait for the queued native close event delivery; assert dialog remains open, selected new task/detail loads and new focus is not stolen. Do not dispatch a fake close event, suppress the listener or wait before reopen.
minimalDesignCandidate: An old close observation must not clear the current open dialog. Owner can use current open/generation state, keeping ordinary final-close invalidation and return focus. Existing openTask already invalidates prior detail authority. No source edits performed by root.
